proposition: For one frozen governed exact same-unit finite-state surface, a lossless reusable or regenerable carrier plus outcome-independent dynamic typed enumeration preserves every discoverable exact conjunction, minority, contradiction, and counterpattern fact available from a persistent configuration index; motif, topology, or geometry indexes add constitutive empirical content only when they introduce an explicit new relation/equivalence commitment.
why_high_information: Directly tests whether the remaining reason to keep configuration-like persistence is unknown-claim discovery rather than known-claim truth; controls the largest possible grammar simplification.
current_evidence: Canary1 proves information breadth beyond direct claim sufficiency; canary2 proves carrier truth increment can be zero while replay value is real; neither tests unknown-claim discovery equivalence.
what_would_defeat_or_weaken_it: A lawful pattern or claim candidate discoverable from a persistent/indexed object but not reproducibly enumerable from the carrier under the same authority/loss ceiling; or required discovery latency/feasibility shown to be a constitutive consumer requirement rather than engineering preference.
authority_or_evidence_needed: Frozen discovery-surface definition; admissible enumeration family; sparse/abstention law; outcome-independent evaluation rule; governed same-unit carrier.

proposition: If ephemeral and materialized realizations bind identical common input, semantic identity, relation commitment, loss ceiling, and query-interface obligations, physical persistence or storage layout alone does not create a distinct admissible object specification.
why_high_information: Could collapse a large class of false object multiplicity immediately and makes physical architecture neutral without deleting replay value.
current_evidence: Strongly supported by W1 versus W4/W3 second-canary rulings, FFIF008 reversible encoding law, and FFIF010 PERSISTENT_VS_EPHEMERAL_STORAGE_DIFFERENCE != AOS_DIFFERENCE.
what_would_defeat_or_weaken_it: A case where persistence itself changes a constitutive empirical invariant, admissible query interface, provenance/recoverability ceiling, or semantic relation rather than only cost/latency.
authority_or_evidence_needed: Primarily adjudicative specification work; consumer contract needed if persistence is claimed constitutive.

proposition: For any future local-location claim, a lawful order/neighborhood relation must be challenged before a cardinal metric relation, and an exact metric relation before low-dimensional coordinates; the stronger layer is claim-necessary only if the proposition contains an invariant unavailable from every lawful weaker layer within CITC.
why_high_information: Discriminates whether geometry survives as one architectural primitive or only as a typed ladder of progressively stronger relations.
current_evidence: Canary1 separates exact metric from lossy coordinates and shows most k1 neighborhood mass is same-profile equivalence; canary2 does not require geometry.
what_would_defeat_or_weaken_it: A frozen claim whose cardinal or coordinate invariant cannot be restated or preserved by any weaker order/direct relation and whose stronger relation passes semantic/metric authority and hostile controls.
authority_or_evidence_needed: Lawful order/cardinality/metric authority; locality/domain; PRA/TTAR where invoked; CIM/CITC; observability/connectedness.

proposition: A graph/hypergraph or motif/repertoire artifact is a distinct empirical AOS only when its edge/nonedge, topology, pattern-equivalence, or recurrence relation is itself claim- or discovery-constitutive; materializing an index over already-authorized facts does not create a new primitive.
why_high_information: Separates genuine relation autonomy from useful indexing and protects unknown-claim discovery without promoting graph or motif ontology.
current_evidence: FFIF001 and FFIF007 already type topology/motif as relation families; both genuine canaries show storage is not semantic identity but do not test these relations.
what_would_defeat_or_weaken_it: A bounded discovery/consumer requirement demonstrating that a persistent motif/topology index has constitutive empirical semantics not expressible as the declared edge/pattern relation plus query contract.
authority_or_evidence_needed: Typed edge/nonedge or motif-equivalence authority; support/stability/null law; discovery or claim identity contract.

proposition: Cross-context recurrence should first be represented as independently frozen local invariant objects plus explicit authorized mapping/transport predicates; a separate transport/signature AOS is required only when the bundled recurrence relation is itself constitutive and cannot be decomposed into those interfaces without a new primitive fusion.
why_high_information: Tests whether recurrence needs another persistent world representation or only typed cross-context relation contracts over local objects.
current_evidence: FFIF003/005 support local-first mixed-invariant transport with no common world-space; neither genuine canary tests cross-context recurrence.
what_would_defeat_or_weaken_it: A preregistered recurrence claim where componentwise local invariants plus authorized correspondence cannot express the complete frozen assertion without a new bundled relation.
authority_or_evidence_needed: TTAR/PRA where invoked; mapping-plan freeze; transport CIM/CITC; risk-set/estimand compatibility; negative maps/controls.
